newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET SEEN TIGHT NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET SEEN TIGHT NEXT WEEK.

text.p: Short-term interest rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mostly lower in quiet trade on Friday, but dealers predicted the market may tighten again next week.
"I think things will tighten a bit next week because the (treasury bill) maturities expected are unlikely to provide enough cover," one dealer said.
"The market is on the quiet side today and the rates are generally lower," he added.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 25 percent, down on Thursday's 28 percent level, and being sold at 21 percent from 22 percent while call money was quoted at 15 percent, down from its overnight 20 percent rate.
Bankers' acceptance bills (BAs) were being bought at a stable 22 percent but were selling at 20.25 percent from 21 percent on Thursday.
